body:
FOUND 2026-08-12 by the T35 lane (PR #399), which named it in the spec as a gap rather than closing it. It is the sharpest of the four T35 left open, and it deserves its own shard because it reads as a privilege escalation on the exact surface §24 exists to confine.

WHAT IS WRONG. §24.7 opens the quarantine pool with the primary's pen seeds so that a probationary app can actually WRITE — without that, a stranger's app can only paint a preview, which is the failure clause 1 forbids. But the whole PEN TABLE crosses the boundary, not just the pen that app was granted. So a quarantined renderer — a STRANGER's code, which is the entire premise of §24 — may name any pen the operator has provisioned and write under that author.

WHY IT MATTERS. The confinement story says a stranger's app runs against your real ground VISIBLY ON PROBATION, and that what keeps that safe is the operator can still forget (erasure fans out) and still cap the bill (T34's envelope). Authorship is the third leg: writes from the pool are supposed to be attributable to the probationary app, under its own granted author, so a reader can tell whose claim is whose. If any pen can be named, that attribution is a guess. The bytes still land in a droppable pool and never canonical — that containment holds — but WHO the pool says wrote them is no longer trustworthy.

MEASURE FIRST, and this one has a sharp experiment: provision two pens, put a renderer in a quarantine pool granted only the first, and have it name the second. If it writes, the escalation is real and the ticket is confirmed; if something already refuses, find what and say so, and close this.

THE REPAIR, if measurement earns it: the pool receives only the pens its own renderer was granted, never the table. The natural shape is to pass a NARROWED map at pool open rather than filtering at use — a filter at use is one forgotten call site away from being no filter at all, and this is the class where that costs authorship.

RELATED GAP, same slice: a pen granted ONLY inside the quarantine is refused, which makes the safer-looking configuration the refused one. Fixing this ticket well probably fixes that too; if the two pull apart, say so rather than bundling them.

RAILS: two-sided at both levels — the granted pen writes and its delta carries that author, AND naming a pen the renderer was not granted refuses, with the refusal naming nothing about what else exists (a refusal that enumerates the pen table would hand a stranger the map it was denied).

WHO MERGES: MYK. It narrows a capability on the confinement surface, and §24 is the section whose whole subject is what a stranger's code may do.
title: The whole pen table crosses into a quarantine pool — a stranger's renderer may write as ANY provisioned pen
